summary:
**LunaRIDGE — Lunar Radio Illumination and Direct Geometry Evaluator**

LunaRIDGE is an interactive lunar mission-planning tool designed to help users evaluate potential landing locations and mission dates near the Moon's South Pole.

The application combines NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data with NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) terrain elevation data to calculate terrain-aware direct Earth visibility and sunlight availability.

Users can explore lunar regions, evaluate communication and illumination windows, compare multiple scenarios, search for promising candidate locations and dates, and generate scientific PDF reports.

LunaRIDGE supports early-stage mission planning by turning complex NASA scientific data into accessible visualizations and explainable assessments. It is a research prototype and does not claim to predict complete radio-link performance, electrical power generation or landing safety.
details:
LunaRIDGE — Lunar Radio, Illumination and Direct-to-Earth Geometry Evaluator

The Problem

Planning operations near the Moon's South Pole requires understanding when a spacecraft can receive sunlight and maintain a direct geometric view of Earth. Mountains, crater walls and changing celestial geometry make these conditions strongly dependent on the selected location and mission dates.

Our Solution

LunaRIDGE is an interactive web-based scientific prototype that helps users evaluate lunar South Pole locations and mission windows.

Instead of manually combining multiple scientific datasets, users can explore candidate regions, configure mission scenarios and obtain understandable Earth-visibility and sunlight-availability results.

How It Works

LunaRIDGE combines two NASA resources:

NASA JPL Horizons: Provides the predicted directions of Earth and the Sun relative to the selected lunar location over time.

NASA LRO/LOLA Terrain Data: Provides lunar topographic information used to estimate the surrounding terrain skyline.

The application compares the predicted elevation of Earth or the Sun with the modeled local terrain-horizon elevation. Repeating this analysis across a selected UTC interval produces visibility windows, interruption durations and summary percentages.

Main Features

  • Explore Moon: Interactive lunar South Pole map and candidate location selection.
  • Mission Planner: Configure locations, dates, observer height and scientific analysis settings.
  • Results: Examine geometric Earth visibility, sunlight availability, timelines and terrain-related diagnostics.
  • Mission Assessment: Check four configurable visibility and interruption requirements.
  • Scenario Comparison: Compare two to five locations or mission intervals using shared requirements, with Simple and Engineering views.
  • Opportunity Finder: Search bounded sets of candidate locations or dates to identify useful visibility opportunities.
  • Recommended Examples: Explore recorded, validated scenarios without immediately requiring a new NASA ephemeris request.
  • Scientific Reporting: Download PDF reports documenting scenario inputs, results, assumptions and references.

Technologies Used

The application uses:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI.
  • Astronomical Data: NASA JPL Horizons.
  • Lunar Terrain Data: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter / Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LRO/LOLA).
  • AI-Assisted Development Tools: Google Antigravity, OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT.

NASA JPL Horizons supplies astronomical ephemerides, while NASA LOLA digital elevation data supports terrain-aware geometric calculations.

Results and Validation

Selected lunar South Pole scenarios were tested against independently configured NASA Horizons references and separate terrain-geometry calculations.

For example, an evaluation of the Haworth area over a 492-hour November 2026 interval produced 27.93% modeled direct Earth-center visibility and 0% Sun-center visibility under the specified model settings.

These results demonstrate how local terrain and observation timing can affect potential communication and illumination opportunities.

Automated backend and frontend test suites were used to check scientific processing, application behavior, scenario comparison and reporting functionality.

Innovation and Impact

LunaRIDGE's contribution is bringing terrain-aware geometry, NASA scientific datasets, explainable mission requirements, scenario comparison and bounded opportunity searching into one accessible workflow.

Instead of treating lunar location and mission timing as separate decisions, LunaRIDGE allows users to explore their combined effects through a unified interface.

The application is intended to support education, scientific exploration and early-stage lunar mission-planning studies.

Limitations and Future Development

LunaRIDGE evaluates modeled geometric visibility. It does not guarantee radio communication, calculate actual electrical energy generation or certify landing safety.

Results depend on terrain-model coverage, search radius, spatial resolution and time sampling.

Future development could include detailed RF link-budget analysis, solar-array and battery modeling, expanded validation and more comprehensive candidate-site searches.

AI-Assisted Development and Transparency

Artificial intelligence tools were used during the development of LunaRIDGE, including Google Antigravity, OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT.

These tools assisted with software implementation, code generation and refinement, debugging, test development, interface design, documentation and technical explanations.

The project was developed through an AI-assisted workflow involving human direction, review and testing. Scientific calculations were evaluated using automated tests, selected independently configured NASA Horizons reference comparisons and separate terrain-geometry checks.

AI assistance is acknowledged transparently rather than presenting all generated code and content as manually authored.

Any AI-generated presentation illustrations or other visual assets included in the final submission are identified in accordance with the competition's disclosure requirements.

LunaRIDGE remains a scientific software prototype with explicitly documented assumptions, limitations and validation scope.
